title: Caleb and the Giant Grapes
summary: Twelve spies set out to see the Land of Israel and come back with an enormous cluster of grapes. Ten of them are afraid, but Caleb and Joshua see the good and call out, "We can do it!" A story about courage, optimism and how we look at new things.
pages:
The Children of Israel had almost reached the Land of Israel.
"What does it look like?" everyone asks.
Moses sends twelve men to see. One of them is Caleb.

Caleb fills a backpack, and so does his friend Joshua.
They walk through mountains, through fields, beside streams.
What a land! Everything is green, and there are flowers everywhere.

Beside one stream they find a cluster of grapes. Giant!
So big that it takes two men to carry it on a pole.
They pick pomegranates and figs too.

But there are scary things in the land too.
Cities with high, high walls,
and people as big as giants.

Caleb goes alone to Hebron, the place of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
There he prays quietly: "God, give me courage."

The spies return, and all the people gather.
Ten spies say: "The land is good, but we can't do it. The people there are giants, and next to them we are like little grasshoppers!"

The people are frightened. Grown-ups cry, and children too.
"Oh no, what will we do?"

But Caleb raises his hand. "Shhh... quiet!"
Everyone looks at him.
"Let us go up!" he calls. "We can do it!"
And Joshua stands beside him. "The land is very, very good," he says. "And God is with us. Don't be afraid!"

But the people are still afraid. The time hasn't come yet.
The Children of Israel must wait in the desert, to grow and become stronger.

And Caleb waits patiently.
He knows that one day he will go back to Hebron and live there with his family.

New things happen to you too: a new preschool, a new friend, a food you've never tasted.
You can see only the high walls, or you can also see the sweet grapes.
And you can say, like Caleb: We can do it!
